Assessment incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Policy stance remains highly accommodative (ZLB, outcome-based forward guidance, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases, repos/ON RRP), supporting market functioning and compressing term premia.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks reported tightened lending standards across many categories through Q3 2020, with demand patterns bifurcated:
  - Stronger demand and originations concentrated in GSE-eligible and QM non-jumbo mortgages; MBS purchases reinforce this channel.
  - Weaker demand and tighter conditions for subprime mortgages and commercial real estate; CRE stress and CMBS delinquencies persist.
  - Forbearance policies and bank capital/liquidity positions influenced lending practices; profitability pressures remain a headwind.
- Implication: Despite easy financial conditions and effective market backstops, bank credit supply to riskier borrowers and CRE remains constrained, muting transmission to the broader economy. Strength in housing offsets some weakness, but business credit and CRE weigh on the outlook.
- Net read: Compared with the FSR-only view, the SLOOS points to a more uneven and restrictive bank-credit channel, nudging risk balance slightly more negative than before.
